questions.q: Erikson's first psychosocial crisis, occurring in infancy, is
questions.e: In infancy the child develops trust if caregivers are reliable and responsive. Autonomy vs shame follows in early childhood.

questions.q: Object permanence is acquired in Piaget's ______ stage.
questions.e: In the sensorimotor stage (birth to about 2 years), infants learn that objects continue to exist when out of sight.

questions.q: The theory of multiple intelligences was proposed by
questions.e: Howard Gardner (1983) proposed several relatively independent intelligences, such as linguistic, logical-mathematical and musical.

questions.q: Which parenting style combines warmth and responsiveness with firm limits?
questions.e: Authoritative parents are warm and explain rules while setting clear limits. Authoritarian parents are strict and low in warmth.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kohlberg's theory of moral development.
I. It has three levels, each with two stages.
II. The law-and-order orientation belongs to the conventional level.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The pre-conventional, conventional and post-conventional levels together hold six stages. Stage 4, law and order, falls in the conventional level.

questions.q: A child with chronological age 10 years has a mental age of 12 years. Using the ratio formula, the child's IQ is
G. Stanley Hall described adolescence as a period of
questions.e: Hall, drawing on the German phrase Sturm und Drang, viewed adolescence as a turbulent period of emotional ups and downs.

questions.q: Which statement best reflects the accepted modern view of heredity and environment in child development?
o: Development is the result of continuous interaction between heredity and environment
questions.e: Heredity sets potentials and environment shapes how they are expressed, so the two interact throughout development.

questions.q: Match the stage of life with Erikson's psychosocial crisis.
questions.e: Infancy: trust vs mistrust. Early childhood: autonomy vs shame and doubt. School years: industry vs inferiority. Adolescence: identity vs role confusion.

questions.q: A child who calls every four-legged animal a 'dog' is told that a cow is not a dog, and then forms a new category for cows. In Piaget's terms, forming the new category is
questions.e: Accommodation is changing or creating schemas to fit new information. Assimilation fits new input into an existing schema, as when the cow was first called a dog.
